jobs.title: Project Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
:
**GFT** is seeking a **Project Environmental Scientist** to join our growing Environmental Practice! This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring regular attendance at either our **Berkeley, CA or Roseville, CA** offices.  

GFT’s Environmental team delivers integrated planning, permitting, and compliance solutions that support infrastructure development across North America. With more than 140 professionals in 22 offices, the team guides clients through NEPA and permitting processes, ecological and regulatory assessments, and environmental remediation efforts. Their expertise spans transportation, power, water, and facilities markets — working alongside agencies at federal, state, and local levels. From stream restoration to complex regulatory requirements and advance critical infrastructure projects. **What you’ll be challenged to do:**
This is an excellent career opportunity for an experienced, motivated Project Environmental Scientist who is ready to take the next step in their career. We are looking for someone how combines strong technical permitting expertise – a professional that enjoys doing the work, working directly with clients and regulatory agencies and helping to building a growing environmental practice.
The successful candidate will have strong working knowledge of California and federal environmental permitting requirements, particularly as they apply to transportation, water and power projects. This individual will lead and prepare permit applications and technical documentation, coordinate with regulatory agencies, manage permitting assignments and support projects through planning and through design and construction. **In this capacity, the successful candidate will be responsible for the following:*** Lead and support natural resource analysis and environmental permitting for transportation, water, and other infrastructure projects throughout California.
* Develop permitting strategies and identify federal, state, and local regulatory requirements during project planning, CEQA/NEPA and design.
* Prepare and manage permit applications and supporting technical documentation, including Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, and other applicable federal, state, and local permits and approvals.
* Coordinate directly with regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, California Department of Fish and Wildlife, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, NOAA Fisheries, and other agencies as appropriate.
* Conduct wetland delineations, jurisdictional assessments, biological field studies, and other technical investigations necessary to support project permitting as well as CEQA/NEPA analysis.
* Author and review technical reports, CEQA/NEPA analysis, permit applications, environmental commitments, mitigation plans, and related environmental deliverables.
* Work closely with engineering and design teams to identify natural resource and permitting constraints, develop practical avoidance and minimization measures, and incorporate environmental requirements into project design and construction.
* Support environmental compliance during construction, including implementation and tracking of permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
* Manage environmental permitting assignments, including scope, schedule, budget, staffing, deliverables, and client communications.
* Contribute to and increasingly lead environmental components of proposals, interviews, scopes of work, and cost estimates.
* Contribute to the continued development of GFT’s California Environmental Practice.


:
**What you will bring to our firm:*** Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, the physical sciences, or closely related field.
* Approximately 5\-8 years of progressively responsible experience, with significant experience delivering natural resources and permitting services for infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated experience preparing and managing environmental permits for projects in California.
* Strong working knowledge of applicable federal and California environmental regulations.
* Experience working with and developing relationships with regulatory agencies such as USACE, CDFW, RWQCB, USFWA and/or NOAA Fisheries.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Self\-starter, able to complete tasks with minimal supervision and direction.
* Willingness to travel and execute work in a variety of settings and environmental conditions (heat, cold, rain, etc.).
* Demonstrated leadership and interpersonal skills to work effectively with others and achieve results.
* Demonstrated agility working with multi\-disciplined infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated professional judgment, consistency, strong attention to detail, and background of high\-quality work products.
* Ability to prepare and deliver presentations and lead meetings, when needed.
* An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in helping grow a developing California environmental practice.

**What we prefer you bring:*** A Master’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology or a closely related field.
* Established relationships with California transportation agencies, water agencies, municipalities, regulatory agencies, or other infrastructure clients.
* Experience with Caltrans, local transportation agencies, passenger rail/transit agencies, water districts, utilities, or similar California public\-sector clients.
* GIS experience.
* Relevant professional certifications or specialized permitting/natural\-resource credentials.

### **Compensation:**


The salary range for this role is **$95,000 \- $135,000**; Salary is dependent upon experience and geographic location.### **Featured Benefits:**

* Hybrid (in\-person and remote) work environment.
* Comprehensive benefits package including wellness programs, parental leave, and pet insurance, in addition to medical, dental,

jobs.title: Environmental Science Senior II - (Major Projects)
jobs.description:
**About Us**SoCalGas, the nation's largest gas distribution utility, is dedicated to providing safe, reliable, and affordable energy to over 21 million Southern California customers. Through innovation, collaboration, and an unwavering commitment to the needs of our communities we proudly uphold our mindset of “Glad to be of Service” and provide exceptional customer service today and ready to meet California's energy needs with innovative solutions for tomorrow.
As an employee of SoCalGas, you will support our core values to do the right thing, champion people, and shape the future. You will play a pivotal role in the energy transition initiatives, supporting our mission: Safe, reliable, and affordable energy delivery today. Ready for tomorrow. We are committed to attracting top talent and fostering a diverse workforce that reflects the vibrant communities we serve.
As an employee of SoCalGas, you'll enjoy a competitive compensation plan, upward mobility opportunities and the ability to find a true work life balance. Discover the rewards of joining SoCalGas by exploring our website: Our Mission; Sustainability, In the Community, and Employee Benefits. Join SoCalGas today and become a vital part of a team that is driving innovation, championing community needs, and shaping the future of energy in California.
**Primary Purpose**
Applies specialized knowledge to lead functional projects and secure cost‑effective compliance. Independently develops innovative approaches and engages regulators on technical matters.
**Team \& Role Context**
The Environmental Science Senior II is a senior level role on a team of environmental professionals in the Environmental Services Department at SoCalGas. The team's primary role is to support Company infrastructure projects with environmental and regulatory permitting and entitlements, which may include CEQA and NEPA environmental review. Teamwork and cross functional collaboration are central to the team's approach, working closely with project managers, technical experts, stakeholder engagement leads, agency partners and the public. This team is involved with project feasibility studies, permit application preparation and submittal, agency coordination and public outreach, environmental review and construction compliance monitoring. Working independently with guidance only in the most complex situations, the Senior II leads the environmental evaluation and permitting activities of complex projects and possesses specialized knowledge of environmental science, including one or more environmental disciplines, such as land use planning, biology, archaeology, air quality or related fields.  

**Duties and Responsibilities**
* Act as the environmental lead and coordinate studies, review documents, and implement compliance measures \& training. Identify / address environmental requirements including federal \& state regulatory requirements, permit conditions, avoidance \& mitigation measures related to infrastructure projects
* Provide technical leadership for environmental documents, which may include CEQA/NEPA, permit applications, and project deliverables.
* Coordinate and/or participate in field activities, including construction compliance monitoring and environmental inspections. Prepare permitting schedules, integrates with project plans, evaluates risks, and communicates with stakeholders and management.
* Executes programs to ensure regulatory obligations are met while optimizing costs and minimizing operational disruptions.
* Provides technical expertise in leveraging GIS data for spatial analysis and visualization, ensuring adherence to industry standards and best practices.
* Monitors day\-to\-day environmental compliance programs including waste management, water pollution control, spill plans and response, emergency planning and release reporting, and other applicable environmental requirements.
* Reviews environmental record keeping and reporting including data review and analysis, report preparation, report filing, agency notification, permit application review and input to regulatory comments.
* Leads the development of environmental processes, procedures and environmental awareness training.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
Requirements:
**Education**
* Required: a 4 year degree in a relevant field, or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Preferred: Degree, preferably in environmental studies/science, urban/environmental planning, biology, anthropology/archaeology, geography, engineering, or related field. Master's degree is preferred.

  


  

**Experience**
* Required: 8 years of related experience.
* Preferred: Experience with project scope analysis to determine applicable regulations and permits; development of permitting strategies; management and review of technical reports, permit applications, and environmental documents (e.g., CEQA, NEPA); and development of environmental schedules is preferred.

  


  

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**
* Required: Ability to anticipate emerging environmental risks and trends.
* Required: Ability to balance scientific rigor with regulatory and business constraints.
* Required: Ability to operate autonomously on high\-visibility scientific initiatives.
* Required: Knowledge of advanced environmental science methodologies and assessment frameworks.
* Required: Knowledge of cumulative impact analysis and risk evaluation techniques.
* Required: Skill in leading complex investigations, modeling efforts, or impact assessments.
* Required: Skill in synthesizing diverse datasets to support environmental decision\-making.
* Preferred: Strong project management skills with the ability to review complex problems and propose innovative solutions. Experience managing requirements of complex projects including design requirements, schedule, budget, and differing stakeholder interests. Capable of coordinating with diverse groups of stakeholders. jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist IV
jobs.description:
**Position Description**
------------------------

  

  

**SUMMARY OF POSITION**
The Environmental Health Bureau sits within the County of Monterey’s Department of Health and consists of seven major environmental health regulatory programs: Healthy Housing Services, Consumer Health Protection Services, Drinking Water Protection Services, Environmental Health Review (Land Use) Services, Hazardous Materials Management Services, Recycling and Resource Recovery Services, and Solid Waste Management Services.  

  

The Environmental Health Bureau is seeking to fill one full\-time Environmental Health Specialist IV (EHS IV) for the Healthy Housing Services program.  

  

The Healthy Housing Services program is responsible for ensuring safe and healthy living environments through the inspection and enforcement of state and local housing regulations for residential rental housing, employee housing, detention facilities, and other regulated facilities. The program investigates housing complaints, addresses substandard housing conditions, conducts vector control and agricultural field toilet inspections, supports the Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Program, and performs other environmental health activities designed to protect community health and prevent environmental health hazards.  

  

The EHS IV is a supervisory/leadership position whose primary responsibility is to actively support the Director of Environmental Health's goals and vision by performing supervisory tasks such as administrative oversight and quality assurance of environmental health programs. Subordinate staff provide enforcement of environmental public health laws by conducting field inspections, project reviews and report writing. This role is to ensure activities are completed by providing timely feedback to staff while reviewing their work, spotting trends, and ensuring proper follow\-up. The EHS IV guides the team to effectively meet performance measures and maintain high standards of practice. Several programs also include grant funded projects where substantive administrative, contract policy and technical issues require specialized analysis, strategic planning, stakeholder collaboration, program recommendation and public outreach. This position is responsible for managing their program by utilizing team resources efficiently, thorough planning, delegating tasks to staff, monitoring progress and frequent communication.  

  

**As of October 11, 2023, the Health Department offers up to a $10,000 signing bonus to candidates hired into regular full\-time positions for this classification from this recruitment.**  

  

*The County of Monterey is committed to honoring the service and sacrifice of veterans and eligible military spouses and awards veterans’ preference points for this recruitment. To learn more about the eligibility requirements and the process, be sure to read the* ***Hiring Preference for Veterans******and Eligible Military Spouses*** *section located towards the end of this job flyer.*  

  

*The Eligible List established by this recruitment process will be used to fill current and future vacancies, both regular and temporary, as they arise.*
**Examples of Duties**
----------------------


* Plans, schedules, assigns and evaluates the work of an environmental health staff; reviews inspection and investigation reports prepared by staff.
* In a geographic district, represents the Division in all program areas to public bodies and private groups within the district; performs inspections and investigations as necessary, acts as a liaison to a variety of agencies on matters relating to the district.
* Monitors and coordinates the inspection, investigation and enforcement activities of the staff; accompanies staff in field investigations to insure consistency, completeness and conformity to laws and regulations.
* Trains staff in all laws, ordinances and regulations, policies and procedures relating to environmental health programs.
* Develops, interprets and implements policies, regulations, procedures and programs for the unit or district; identifies operational problems and recommends solutions.
* May perform the most complex and sensitive investigations or studies involving potential violations of environmental health laws, rules and regulations; prepares reports of findings, recommends legal action and prepares materials for use in legal actions.
* May act as liaison to other governmental agencies and represents the Division in responding to inquiries or providing information to the public, business and other interested groups.

  

**Physical and Sensory Requirements:**
* Tolerate rodents and insects such as rates, mice and cockroaches; and substandard dwellings with unsanitary or hazardous conditions such as septic failures, accumulated garbage or animal waste.
* Work with potentially hostile individuals in volatile situations.

To view the complete job description, please visit the Monterey County website: Environmental Health Specialist IV  

  

**THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE**
Will have a proven track record demonstrating the following knowledge, skills, and abilities:  

  

**Thorough Knowledge of:**
* Federal, state and local laws, regulations and procedures governing environmental health.
* Principles, methods, technology and equipment applied in inspection, analysis and enforcement of environmental health regulations.
* Principles and practices of effective supervision.
  
  

**Working Knowledge of:**
* Engineering, chemistry, microbiology, biology, epidemiology, hydrology and geology relating to environmental health programs.

* Write effectively to prepare complex written reports, correspondence and memoranda.
* Speak effectively to individuals and groups.

jobs.title: Transfer - Principal Air Quality Chemist
jobs.description:
**SOUTH COAST AQMD AND JOB OVERVIEW**
-------------------------------------


**This is a transfer opportunity, open only to current South Coast AQMD employees, and is expected to result in a transfer list from which current and future Principal Air Quality Chemist vacancies may be filled.**  

  

Please note that a transfer application, once accepted, is active for six calendar months.
**EXAMPLE OF DUTIES**
---------------------


To view the classification specification, click the link here.
* Plans, organizes, and supervises the work of staff assigned to a laboratory section involved in qualitative and quantitative analyses to isolate, identify, and quantify air contaminants; reviews requests for analyses, determines the level of difficulty, and assigns work; and provides technical and administrative guidance to professional and technical staff and evaluates performance.
* Develops, supervises, prioritizes, and evaluates programs and projects; maintains workload statistics on unit activities; prepares program\- and activity\-related reports and analyses; reviews and edits technical reports prepared by laboratory staff to ensure accuracy of data, appropriateness of methodologies, and soundness of findings and conclusions; and identifies and maintains data quality objectives on a program basis.
* Serves as a technical expert and resource for South Coast AQMD staff regarding chemistry\-related air quality matters and on a variety of technical advisory committees; maintains a broad understanding of current research into causes, sources, and chemical reactions contributing to air quality problems; and consults with outside experts regarding air quality issues relevant to laboratory programs and projects.
* Applies professional training and experience and keeps abreast of updated and new chemical laboratory methods, instrumentation, protocols, and practices through review of professional literature and other research resources and evaluates staff recommendations to ensure the laboratory uses the most effective and up\-to\-date techniques in analyzing air contaminants, accomplishing the work of the unit, and meeting new or changing South Coast AQMD rules
* Reviews and approves test methods used by private laboratories for compliance with South Coast AQMD rules.
* Represents South Coast AQMD at scientific conferences and prepares for publication and presents research reports and papers on methods, procedures, results, and conclusions relating to laboratory analyses.
* Testifies in court and before public bodies and hearing boards.
* Prepares annual budget request for the section and submits written justification for budget items requested; and is responsible for the preparation of grant proposals for federal government or other funding.
* Acts for the laboratory services manager, as needed.
**MINIMUM AND DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------------------


**ELIGIBILITY**


* Must currently be in the Principal Air Quality Chemist classification.

**OR**
* To transfer to a new class title, your current classification must have the exact same pay and you must complete the application demonstrating that you meet the minimum requirements for the new class.

**Please note:** To transfer, an employee must have passed probation (12\-month initial probation or 6\-month promotional probation).


**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**


**EDUCATION:** Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in chemistry, preferably with an emphasis in qualitative and quantitative analysis.


**EXPERIENCE:** One year as a Senior Air Quality Chemist or three years as an Air Quality Chemist or equivalent.


**KNOWLEDGE OF:** Current methods, procedures, protocols, and instrumentation relating to organic, inorganic, and physical qualitative and quantitative analysis; operational principles of relevant chemical laboratory instrumentation and techniques; principles and practices of project management, supervision, training, and budgeting; relevant professional research literature and resources; principles and methods of statistical analysis; working knowledge of database design, information management, and computer programming, as they relate to laboratory analysis of air contaminants; safety procedures and practices relating to laboratory work; PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; professional report writing; South Coast AQMD rules and federal and State laws related to chemical analysis of air contaminants; and protocols and standards for laboratory analysis of air quality samples.


**SKILL OR ABILITY TO:** Supervise, evaluate, train, and assign work to professional and technical staff involved in routine and complex qualitative and quantitative organic, inorganic and physical analysis of air quality samples; effectively use available resources in planning and organizing programs and projects; evaluate the effectiveness of programs and projects in meeting laboratory and overall South Coast AQMD objectives; oversee the development and implementation of new laboratory methods, procedures, and protocols, the adaptation of existing instrumentation and methods for new purposes, and the evaluation of new instrumentation; understand and interpret applicable laws, rules, and regulations; edit and write detailed, accurate reports on laboratory projects, analyses, methodologies, findings, and conclusions; prepare funding proposals; read, understand, and follow verbal and written directions; proficiently use PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; and establish and maintain effective relationships with all those contacted in the course of work.
  

  

**LICENSE:** Possession of a valid California Class "C" Driver's License and a good driving record may be required.

jobs.company: South Coast Air Quality Management District
jobs.title: Transfer - Assistant/Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
**SOUTH COAST AQMD AND JOB OVERVIEW**
-------------------------------------


**This is a transfer opportunity, open only to current South Coast AQMD employees, and is expected to result in a transfer list from which current and future Assistant** **Air Quality Specialist** **or Air Quality Specialist vacancies may be filled.**  

  

Please note that a transfer application, once accepted, is active for six calendar months.
**EXAMPLE OF DUTIES**
---------------------


To view the classification specification, click the link here.


* Works with engineers, planners, other environmental professionals, Information Management staff, and other personnel to develop and implement methods and techniques for the analysis and evaluation of air quality studies and plans.
* Applies mathematical, statistical, and engineering modeling and analytical techniques to the analysis of research and survey data; prepares graphs, charts, and statistical summaries from derived data; determines appropriate data collection methods for use in research projects; and may assist in determining methods for more complex studies.
* Assists in developing or develops recommendations concerning air quality management programs, plans, and rules and prepares related reports and correspondence.
* Assists in preparing technical analyses and recommended positions on proposed and pending legislation relating to air quality management.
* Reviews and analyzes a wide variety of environmental documents; conducts air quality impact analyses and assessments; and writes or coordinates the writing of Environmental Impact Reports.
* Evaluates economic impacts of air quality regulations and develops economic incentives to achieve designated air quality standards.
* May assist in organizing and participating in workshops and meetings, and provide consultation and advice to individuals and businesses in matters related to area of expertise.
* May assist in preparing and making presentations on proposed rules, rule amendments and other air quality\-related projects and studies.
**MINIMUM AND DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------------------


**ELIGIBILITY**


* Must currently be in the Assistant Air Quality Specialist or Air Quality Specialist classification.

**OR**
* To transfer to a new class title, your current classification must have the exact same pay and you must complete the application demonstrating that you meet the minimum requirements for the new class.

**Please note:** To transfer, an employee must have passed probation (12\-month initial probation or 6\-month promotional probation).


**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**
**EDUCATION:**


Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in engineering, environmental science, planning, or the physical, social, or biological sciences, depending upon the functions of the assigned unit.


**EXPERIENCE:**


**ASSISTANT AIR****QUALITY SPECIALIST:** No experience is required.


**AIR****QUALITY SPECIALIST:** Two years of technical air quality or professional analytical experience that would demonstrate the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities of the position to which assigned.  

  



**KNOWLEDGE OF:** One or more professional disciplines, such as chemistry, toxics, statistics, economics, environmental planning, or engineering, with emphasis on its relationship to planning, rule development, or engineering activities; principles, methods, and procedures of environmental review, planning, rule development, or air quality monitoring, including related instrumentation; air quality regulations and review process; air quality modeling; emissions calculations; PC software applications commonly used in the field; research methods and techniques, including statistical and computer applications for data analysis; professional report writing; and State, federal, and local programs, guidelines, and code regulations related to air quality management.


**SKILL OR ABILITY TO:** Compile, analyze, and interpret technical air quality data; learn and apply South Coast AQMD air quality regulations to stationary and mobile source monitoring; monitor and evaluate the performance of consultants; oversee stationary and mobile source monitoring projects under minimum supervision; maintain accurate records of air quality planning, research, monitoring, or rule development projects and prepare clear and persuasive reports and recommendations; represent South Coast AQMD interests at public, professional, and internal meetings and communicate with a variety of technical and professional air quality and legal staff; maintain current knowledge of applicable federal, State, and local regulations and technical or scientific developments; provide expert testimony, advice, and counsel in a specialized field; apply appropriate computer\-based analytical techniques to complex air pollution control problems; develop new techniques and approaches to the solution of complex air pollution control problems; proficiently use PC and mainframe software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; read, understand, and follow verbal and written directions; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; and establish and maintain effective relationships with all those contacted in the course of work.


  
**PROFESSIONAL EMPLOYEE BENEFIT OVERVIEW**
***BENEFIT***
***DESCRIPTION***
***Monthly Benefit Allotment***
$2,022, to purchase medical, dental, and life insurance, with unused portion paid to you as cash. Your insurance coverage becomes effective on the first of the month following completion of 30 days of continuous service. ----------------


Class Code 28958: Environmental Specialist IV
  

  

**Transfer job postings are for County of Sacramento employees only.**  

**In order to be qualified for a transfer:**
  

1\. You must meet the Minimum Qualifications of the new job.
  

2\. The difference between the top salary steps (the highest pay rate within the range of pay) of your current job class and the job class that you intend to transfer into, must be less than 5%.
  

  

There are three different transfer types that you may qualify for: interdepartmental transfer, interclass transfer, and voluntary demotion. These different transfer types are defined as:


* **Interdepartmental transfer** \- a transfer in the same class from one County department to another.

jobs.title: Senior Hazardous Materials Consultant
jobs.description:
* Role with genuine project ownership \& technical responsibility
* Company Vehicle, competitive salary, overtime
* Strong career development with the backing of global Kiwa group


  

Kiwa ELS is a customer\-focused, results\-driven risk management consultancy with offices in Brisbane and Sydney. We deliver hazardous materials, occupational hygiene, environmental and risk management consulting services to clients across Australia.  

  

As part of the Kiwa Group—a global leader in testing, inspection and certification with more than 12,000 professionals across 35\+ countries—we offer the backing of an international organisation while maintaining a strong local presence.  

  

Working alongside our NATA\-accredited laboratory, our Hazardous Materials team provides asbestos, mould and hazardous materials management, assessment and advisory services to an established client base across the construction, facilities management, transport, insurance and government sectors.  

  

Due to continued growth, we are seeking a full\-time Senior Hazardous Materials Consultant to join our Brisbane\-based team.  

  

Approximately 60% of your time will be spent on site across Southeast Queensland, undertaking hazardous materials and occupational hygiene work. The remaining 40% will be office\-based and focused on technical reporting, project management, proposals, quality assurance and supporting the development of other consultants. Occasional travel to regional locations and interstate may also be required.  

  

**What you will be doing**  

* Conduct asbestos, mould and hazardous materials surveys across industrial, commercial and residential properties.
* Undertake clearance inspections and airborne asbestos fibre monitoring associated with asbestos removal work.
* Complete contamination and post\-remediation verification assessments for asbestos, mould, moisture and other contaminants.
* Conduct occupational hygiene surveys and monitoring
* Manage projects, including developing scopes of work, preparing fee proposals, coordinating resources and ensuring project objectives and deadlines are achieved.
* Produce clear, accurate hazardous materials and occupational hygiene reports.
* Undertake technical review and quality assurance of reports prepared by other consultants.
* Provide technical guidance, training and mentoring to less experienced consultants.
* Liaise with clients and stakeholders to understand project requirements and provide practical technical advice.
* Perform laboratory analysis, including fibre counting for airborne asbestos, where required.
* Conduct respirator face fit testing when required.
* Ensure client deliverables are completed accurately and within agreed timeframes.
* Quality Assurance support when required

**Why work with us?**  

* Company vehicle provided.
* Competitive salary \& overtime based on your experience.
* Senior position with genuine project ownership and technical responsibility.
* Opportunity to mentor and support the development of other consultants.
* Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
* Kiwa Rewards, including discounts on shopping, travel, insurance and more.
* Access to our Employee Assistance Program.
* Supportive local team with the backing of a global organisation.


  

**Experience and qualifications**  

* 3\+ years’ experience in hazardous materials consulting, occupational hygiene or a closely related field.
* A current LAA licence is essential.
* A current Australian driver’s licence is essential.
* Science, environmental or hazardous materials qualifications, including relevant P\-Certs, are desirable.
* Professional membership with AIOH, FAMANZ or a similar industry body will be highly regarded.
* Demonstrated experience preparing and reviewing technical reports.
* Experience managing projects, developing scopes and preparing fee proposals will be highly regarded.

**About you**  

* Strong asbestos and/or Occ Hygiene background \- Technically strong and confident providing advice to clients, contractors and other consultants.
* Comfortable balancing hands\-on fieldwork with reporting, project management and technical review.
* Well organised and capable of managing multiple projects, priorities and deadlines.
* Able to communicate clearly and professionally with a broad range of stakeholders.
* Confident mentoring and providing constructive technical feedback to other consultants.
* Practical, safety\-focused and detail\-oriented.
* Able to work independently while contributing positively to the wider team.

If you are an experienced hazardous materials professional looking for a senior role that combines fieldwork, project ownership and technical leadership, apply now to join the Kiwa ELS team.

new_jobs.description:
**SOUTH COAST AQMD AND JOB OVERVIEW**
-------------------------------------


**This is a transfer opportunity, open only to current South Coast AQMD employees, and is expected to result in a transfer list from which current and future Principal Air Quality Chemist vacancies may be filled.**  

  

Please note that a transfer application, once accepted, is active for six calendar months.
**EXAMPLE OF DUTIES**
---------------------


To view the classification specification, click the link here.
* Plans, organizes, and supervises the work of staff assigned to a laboratory section involved in qualitative and quantitative analyses to isolate, identify, and quantify air contaminants; reviews requests for analyses, determines the level of difficulty, and assigns work; and provides technical and administrative guidance to professional and technical staff and evaluates performance.
* Develops, supervises, prioritizes, and evaluates programs and projects; maintains workload statistics on unit activities; prepares program\- and activity\-related reports and analyses; reviews and edits technical reports prepared by laboratory staff to ensure accuracy of data, appropriateness of methodologies, and soundness of findings and conclusions; and identifies and maintains data quality objectives on a program basis.
* Serves as a technical expert and resource for South Coast AQMD staff regarding chemistry\-related air quality matters and on a variety of technical advisory committees; maintains a broad understanding of current research into causes, sources, and chemical reactions contributing to air quality problems; and consults with outside experts regarding air quality issues relevant to laboratory programs and projects.
* Applies professional training and experience and keeps abreast of updated and new chemical laboratory methods, instrumentation, protocols, and practices through review of professional literature and other research resources and evaluates staff recommendations to ensure the laboratory uses the most effective and up\-to\-date techniques in analyzing air contaminants, accomplishing the work of the unit, and meeting new or changing South Coast AQMD rules
* Reviews and approves test methods used by private laboratories for compliance with South Coast AQMD rules.
* Represents South Coast AQMD at scientific conferences and prepares for publication and presents research reports and papers on methods, procedures, results, and conclusions relating to laboratory analyses.
* Testifies in court and before public bodies and hearing boards.
* Prepares annual budget request for the section and submits written justification for budget items requested; and is responsible for the preparation of grant proposals for federal government or other funding.
* Acts for the laboratory services manager, as needed.
**MINIMUM AND DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------------------


**ELIGIBILITY**


* Must currently be in the Principal Air Quality Chemist classification.

**OR**
* To transfer to a new class title, your current classification must have the exact same pay and you must complete the application demonstrating that you meet the minimum requirements for the new class.

**Please note:** To transfer, an employee must have passed probation (12\-month initial probation or 6\-month promotional probation).


**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**


**EDUCATION:** Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in chemistry, preferably with an emphasis in qualitative and quantitative analysis.


**EXPERIENCE:** One year as a Senior Air Quality Chemist or three years as an Air Quality Chemist or equivalent.


**KNOWLEDGE OF:** Current methods, procedures, protocols, and instrumentation relating to organic, inorganic, and physical qualitative and quantitative analysis; operational principles of relevant chemical laboratory instrumentation and techniques; principles and practices of project management, supervision, training, and budgeting; relevant professional research literature and resources; principles and methods of statistical analysis; working knowledge of database design, information management, and computer programming, as they relate to laboratory analysis of air contaminants; safety procedures and practices relating to laboratory work; PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; professional report writing; South Coast AQMD rules and federal and State laws related to chemical analysis of air contaminants; and protocols and standards for laboratory analysis of air quality samples.


**SKILL OR ABILITY TO:** Supervise, evaluate, train, and assign work to professional and technical staff involved in routine and complex qualitative and quantitative organic, inorganic and physical analysis of air quality samples; effectively use available resources in planning and organizing programs and projects; evaluate the effectiveness of programs and projects in meeting laboratory and overall South Coast AQMD objectives; oversee the development and implementation of new laboratory methods, procedures, and protocols, the adaptation of existing instrumentation and methods for new purposes, and the evaluation of new instrumentation; understand and interpret applicable laws, rules, and regulations; edit and write detailed, accurate reports on laboratory projects, analyses, methodologies, findings, and conclusions; prepare funding proposals; read, understand, and follow verbal and written directions; proficiently use PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; and establish and maintain effective relationships with all those contacted in the course of work.
  

  

**LICENSE:** Possession of a valid California Class "C" Driver's License and a good driving record may be required.

-------------------------------------

* Works with engineers, planners, other environmental professionals, Information Management staff, and other personnel to develop and implement methods and techniques for the analysis and evaluation of air quality studies and plans.
* Applies mathematical, statistical, and engineering modeling and analytical techniques to the analysis of research and survey data; prepares graphs, charts, and statistical summaries from derived data; determines appropriate data collection methods for use in research projects; and may assist in determining methods for more complex studies.
* Assists in developing or develops recommendations concerning air quality management programs, plans, and rules and prepares related reports and correspondence.
* Assists in preparing technical analyses and recommended positions on proposed and pending legislation relating to air quality management.
* Reviews and analyzes a wide variety of environmental documents; conducts air quality impact analyses and assessments; and writes or coordinates the writing of Environmental Impact Reports.
* Evaluates economic impacts of air quality regulations and develops economic incentives to achieve designated air quality standards.
* May assist in organizing and participating in workshops and meetings, and provide consultation and advice to individuals and businesses in matters related to area of expertise.
* May assist in preparing and making presentations on proposed rules, rule amendments and other air quality\-related projects and studies.

----------------------------------------


**ELIGIBILITY**

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in engineering, environmental science, planning, or the physical, social, or biological sciences, depending upon the functions of the assigned unit.
